title: The Celtic Freeport receives £18.4 million seed capital funding across four projects
content:
The Celtic Freeport receives £18.4 million seed capital funding across four projects TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
The Celtic Freeport receives £18.4 million seed capital funding across four projects
The Celtic Freeport have achieved a milestone following the approval of
£18.4 million in seed capital funding which will span across four projects
supporting infrastructure, unlocking developments and helping attract private
investment across the freeport.
The approved project includes Associated British Ports which has secured
£5 million for its Talbot Wharf project at Port Talbot. The scheme plans
to unlock 9.1 hectares of land for floating offshore wind supply chain
activities.
Neath Port Talbot Council has been awarded £4.2 million towards an £8.4
million project at Waterside Innovation Park. The development will deliver
six business units at Harbourside, Port Talbot.
At Pembroke Port, the Port of Milford Haven has secured £7.2 million for
the first phase of its Criterion Quay development. The project will restore
marine infrastructure, provide additional berthing capacity and create
1.7 hectares of laydown space to support floating offshore wind activity.
A further £2 million has been awarded for the Ledwood Quayside Upgrade
at Pembroke Dock. The project is intended to improve marine access and
support the fabrication and handling of floating offshore wind components.
Chris Martin, Chair of the Celtic Freeport, said: “Approval of this seed
capital funding marks a major step forward for Celtic Freeport. These four
projects will deliver the infrastructure needed to unlock investment, support
high-quality jobs and accelerate economic growth across southwest Wales.”

title: OEG orders three crew transfer vessels from diverse marine
content:
OEG Marine Services and Diverse Marine have announced an expanded partnership
with delivery of the vessels planned throughout 2027.
The order marks the second collaboration between the companies following
the delivery of OEG Fulmar in 2025.
The vessels will be Diverse Marine BREVITY SL Class CTVs designed by Chartwell
Marine. Each vessel will sit at 26 metres in length and a load line length
of less than 24 metres.
Andy Page, Director of Chartwell Marine, said: “innovative vessel design
can improve operational efficiency, flexibility and safety in deep-water
environments. With AR7 unlocking a new wave of vessel activity and investment.”
The first vessel will be equipped with quad Volvo Penta IPS propulsion,
compliant with IMO Tier III emissions standards and fitted with Hull Vane
transom foils. These features have been selected to improve fuel efficiency
during operations.
All three vessels will be built to the same specification, classed by Bureau
Veritas.
Leif Cooper, Director of OEG Marine Services, said: “This contract marks
the second collaboration for OEG with Diverse Marine, and we are pleased
to continue working together to progress our fleet renewal and expansion
program.”
The newbuilds are intended to support offshore wind operations and are
expected to enter service from 2027.

title: Kumagai Gumi joins as new partner for DemoSATH floating wind project
content:
Kumagai Gumi joins as new partner for DemoSATH floating wind project TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
Kumagai Gumi joins as new partner for DemoSATH floating wind project
Kumagai Gumi has joined Saitec and Kansai Electric Power as a partner in
DemoSATH, a floating offshore wind demonstrator, marking the next phase
of the project with a renewed focus on research and innovation.
Developed by Saitec Offshore Technologies, DemoSATH is designed to support
the advancement of floating offshore wind technology and provide operational
insights for the wider industry.
Under the agreement, the partners will continue operating the DemoSATH
prototype at the BiMEP open-sea test site, extending its operational life
through 2027.
The demonstrator consists of a 2 MW wind turbine mounted on a concrete
twin-hull floating structure. Since entering operation, the turbine has
been exposed to challenging offshore conditions, including waves of up
to 13 metres and wind gusts reaching 100 km/h.
According to the announcement, instrumentation installed on the turbine
and the monitoring system, has been used to track operating conditions
and collect performance data. The information gathered has enabled researchers
to compare real-world performance with models.
Kumagai Gumi was selected for its expertise as a general contractor in
the construction sector. The company is expected to contribute to decommissioning
planning and the assessment of construction methods that could support
future commercial deployment of floating offshore wind technology.

title: Sumitomo Electric opens UK’s first HVDC cable factory
content:
Sumitomo Electric Industries has officially opened the UK's first HVDC
subsea cable factory, marking a major step forward in expanding the country's
electricity transmission infrastructure.
Located at the Port of Nigg in Scotland, the state-of-the-art facility
represents a £350 million investment in the local economy, according to
the company.
Osamu Inoue, president of Sumitomo Electric Industries, said: "This
factory will serve as a vital production base supporting the strengthening
of the UK's transmission infrastructure, the expansion of renewable energy
deployment, and the delivery of a stable and reliable energy supply for
generations to come."
The factory will manufacture 525-kV XLPE HVDC subsea transmission cables
and subsea inter-array cables.
Rob McDonald, managing director of SSEN Transmission, said: "The £350
million facility, which will create at least 200 jobs and support hundreds
more across the wider supply chain, demonstrates the scale of opportunity
that comes from investing in the infrastructure needed to deliver clean
power and energy security."
The opening ceremony, held on October 19, follows Sumitomo Electric's announcement
of the project back in 2023.

title: Seaway 7 contract for Berwick Bank B set to support 465 UK jobs
content:
Seaway 7 contract for Berwick Bank B set to support 465 UK jobs TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
Seaway 7 contract for Berwick Bank B set to support 465 UK jobs
A new contract awarded to Seaway 7 for SSE's Berwick
Bank B project
is expected to support nearly 500 skilled offshore wind jobs across Scotland
and the wider UK.
The agreement is estimated to create 465 jobs across northeast Scotland
and throughout the UK as part of SSE's Preferred Supplier Agreement.
This is in addition to the 600 jobs already created for Berwick Bank B,
the majority of which are based in Scotland, as well as the 100 long-term
roles and 30 construction jobs previously announced by SSE.
As part of the new agreement, Seaway 7 will design, supply and install
subsea inter-array cables and offshore wind turbine foundations for the
1.4 GW offshore wind farm.
UK Government Energy Minister Michael Shanks said: "This contract
will support hundreds of jobs and strengthen Scotland's role in the energy
supply chain. It means more opportunities for Scottish workers and more
homegrown power to protect families from the volatility of global fossil
fuel markets."
Scotland's Cabinet Secretary for Economy, Tourism and Transport Stephen
Flynn said: "By matching Scotland's world-class energy expertise with
the opportunities created by offshore wind and renewable energy, we will
deliver lasting economic benefits for generations to come."

title: Is Front-of-the-Meter Power the Next Data Center Play?
content:
Behind-the-meter power has become a popular strategy as data center operators look for ways to expand capacity in regions where grid constraints are slowing growth.
Some data center operators – especially large hyperscalers – are now exploring a reverse approach: front-of-the-meter power. Instead of building generation solely for their own use, they help add power capacity that feeds into the grid itself.
That distinction could matter as electricity availability becomes one of the defining constraints on data center expansion.
What Is Front-of-the-Meter Power?
In the data center context, front-of-the-meter power refers to arrangements in which a data center operator develops or supports power generation capacity that delivers electricity to the grid, rather than reserving that energy exclusively for its own campus.
For example, instead of relying only on on-site backup generation or
dedicated behind-the-meter assets
, a company could build or back a power project that supplies electricity to the broader grid. In return, the operator may gain more reliable access to power in the market where it is expanding.
Related:
The Ripple Effect of Data Center Project Cancellations and Delays
That is what separates front-of-the-meter power from behind-the-meter strategies. Behind-the-meter generation serves a specific facility or campus. Front-of-the-meter generation contributes to overall grid supply.
How New Is the Concept?
The idea is new in one sense and familiar in another.
Large technology companies have been involved in energy infrastructure and grid-related partnerships for years. Hyperscalers like
have worked with utilities and developers on projects intended to support broader power availability, renewable procurement, or grid expansion.
What makes front-of-the-meter distinct is the possibility that data center operators themselves take a more direct role in developing generation assets that serve the grid. That would go beyond simply financing projects or signing power agreements; it would represent a deeper operational stake in energy infrastructure.
This model is also distinct from grid-interactive or
“grid-supportive” data center designs
, in which on-site generation can sometimes help stabilize the grid. In those cases, the primary purpose of the asset is still to support the data center. A front-of-the-meter project is designed from the outset to add supply to the grid.
Why Would Data Center Operators Pursue It?
The clearest benefit is capacity.
If a company helps bring new generation online, it may improve the odds that enough electricity will be available to support future data center development. That is especially important in markets where utilities are warning of long interconnection queues, delayed energization timelines, or broader supply constraints.
Related:
Battery Storage Gains Ground as Data Centers Seek Diesel Alternatives
It’s also worth noting that front-of-the-meter power can involve developing entire power plants, potentially supplying more energy than on-site, behind-the-meter infrastructure, which is usually smaller in scale.
Front-of-the-meter strategies could also offer political and regulatory advantages. Data centers are drawing scrutiny over the impact on local power systems, land use, and electricity prices. A company that is seen as adding grid capacity rather than just consuming it has a stronger response to concerns that new facilities strain public infrastructure.
At the same time, front-of-the-meter power is unlikely to be the simplest or most financially expedient route to expansion. Building or backing generation assets is capital-intensive, operationally complex, and subject to regulatory hurdles. For many operators, behind-the-meter infrastructure or utility partnerships may remain more practical in the near term.
Who Is Actually Doing It?
So far, front-of-the-meter power appears to be more of an emerging strategy than an established industry norm.
Related:
Can Supercapacitors Smooth AI’s Power Swings?
Amazon has been linked
to a possible front-of-the-meter arrangement tied to a large AI data center facility it’s building in Texas. However, public statements suggest the company is still exploring its options rather than committing to a final model. If Amazon moves forward with a structure that directly adds generation to the grid, it could set an important precedent for other hyperscalers.
For now, however, the concept remains in its early stages. Most data center operators are still relying on a mix of utility partnerships, long-term power procurement, energy storage, and behind-the-meter generation rather than directly building grid-serving power plants themselves.
Will Front-of-the-Meter Power Catch On?
That will depend on how severe grid constraints remain, how quickly grid utilities can expand service, and whether hyperscalers see a strategic advantage in taking a more direct role in power development.
If interconnection delays persist and AI-driven demand continues to rise, front-of-the-meter projects may become more attractive, particularly for the largest operators with the capital to support them. If grid conditions ease or public opposition softens, the business case may be less compelling.
Either way, the idea is worth watching. As power becomes a gating factor in digital infrastructure growth, companies seeking to build the next generation of data centers may need to think less like pure real estate developers and more like energy infrastructure partners.

title: Türkiye allows higher-powered batteries behind existing grid connections - Energy Storage
content: Türkiye has changed its rules to allow consumers to install batteries with more power than their contracted grid connection. They must still keep grid imports within the agreed limit and install controls to prevent electricity exports, but the ruling should free businesses to supply more power than their contracted grid limit. The Energy Market Regulatory Authority (EPDK) published the changes on October 19, with immediate effect. Consumers still need approval from their grid operator, and the battery and consumption facility must use the same metering point. Anyone installing a battery above their contracted power limit must fit automatic power controls and an electricity cut-off system. For businesses, this could allow batteries to supply extra power during short peaks in demand without exceeding the site’s grid import limit. The change is strictly in battery power, measured in kW or MW, rather than capacity. A separate amendment has also allowed storage paired with license-exempt generation to be installed without an energy-capacity limit in kWh or MWh. Battery power must still remain at or below the generating plant’s electrical capacity, but developers can add more hours of storage. Separate licensing changes published the same day cover financial guarantees for generation projects with storage. Developers will not receive their guarantees back until the entire generation facility is operating. For refunds relating to individual storage units, the amount will be based on the power of the units that have passed formal acceptance. The changes come as Türkiye develops a substantial pipeline of wind and solar projects with battery storage. EPDK said in February that it had allocated approximately 33 GW to such projects under legislation introduced in 2022. At that point, 23 projects totaling around 1.07 GW had received generation licenses, with some 208 MW operating. title: Akaysha secures $1.2 billion finance package to grow battery platform - Energy Storage
content: Akaysha Energy, the battery storage developer owned by United States investment giant BlackRock, has refinanced its project-level debt into a AUD$1.75 billion (USD 1.22 billion) portfolio-level financing facility that will support the next stage of its Australian growth. The company said the facility refinances existing project-level debt across its Brendale, Orana, Ulinda Park and Elaine battery energy storage systems (BESS) into a single portfolio-level financing structure. The 155 MW / 298 MWh Ulinda Park and 205 MW / 410 MWh Brendale batteries in Queensland, and the 415 MW / 1,660 MWh Orana BESS in New South Wales (NSW) are part of Akaysha’s operational battery energy storage capacity. The 311 MW / 1,244 MWh Elaine BESS is currently being built in Victoria and is on track to complete in the second half of 2027. Andrew Wegman, managing director and chief financial and investment officer at Akaysha, said the financing package has also been designed to provide flexibility as the company progresses an almost 6 GW / 25 GWh development pipeline of large-scale BESS projects across the National Electricity Market (NEM). “This is an important milestone for Akaysha and it was pleasing to see continued strong support from lenders for our operating portfolio, our pipeline and Australia’s energy transition,” he said. “As well as refinancing our existing operating and construction assets, this portfolio-level facility gives us the flexibility to accelerate our next wave of projects while we continue deploying capital where we see the strongest opportunities across the pipeline.” The transaction comes after Akaysha recently achieved full commercial operations at the 850 MW / 1,680 MWh Waratah Super Battery in NSW. Akaysha’s development pipeline includes the 275 MW / 1,100 MWh Deer Park battery project, the 400 MW / 1, 600 MWh Glenrowan, and the 1,000 MW / 4,000 MWh Connewarren BESS project, all in Victoria. It is also progressing the 250 MW / 1,000 MWh Oaky Creek BESS in Queensland and the 100 MW / 200 MWh Palmerston project in Tasmania. The company’s South Australian projects include the 150 MW / 600 MWh Mobilong and 250 MW / 1,000 MWh Brinkworth BESS. The new financing was supported by a consortium of 11 banks, including ANZ, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, BNP Paribas, Bank of China, CIBC, Deutsche Bank, DNB, ING, Mizuho, MUFG and Rabobank. title: Invenergy plans 38 MW solar-plus-storage project in Mexico - Energy Storage
content: Invenergy Solar Development México plans to build a 38 MW solar power plant paired with a 238 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) in Baja California, Mexico, according to an environmental impact statement submitted to the country’s Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources (Semarnat). The proposed Bura Energy Center would occupy approximately 105.86 hectares. Environmental documentation prepared by ERM México in September 2026 covers the solar generation facilities, battery storage, electrical transformation equipment and grid connection infrastructure. The solar plant would comprise 77,832 photovoltaic modules rated at 650 W each, providing approximately 50.59 MWp of nominal capacity. The panels would be mounted on metal structures with horizontal single-axis trackers to adjust their orientation throughout the day. The electrical conversion system would include 11 inverters, while the transformation infrastructure would comprise 27 transformers and a 50 MVA step-up substation, raising voltage from 34.5 kV to 69 kV. A planned 1.6 km overhead transmission line would connect the facility to the La Rumorosa substation operated by Mexico’s state-owned Federal Electricity Commission (CFE). The battery system would comprise 30 lithium-ion battery units, each with a stated nominal capacity of 8.466 MWh, giving approximately 254 MWh of installed direct-current capacity. The planned operational capacity is 238 MWh, equivalent to about six hours of discharge at the plant’s maximum grid injection capacity of 38 MW. Eight 5 MW power conversion systems would manage battery charging and discharging. The design also includes thermal management, state-of-charge monitoring, electrical protection and fire suppression systems. The project documentation allocates approximately 80 hectares to the solar array and 0.88 hectares to battery storage, with additional space for internal roads, operating buildings, the substation and transmission line. Invenergy’s proposed schedule allows 18 months for site preparation and construction. The facility would have an estimated operating life of 30 years, followed by one year for decommissioning. The environmental assessment identifies 105.86 hectares of forest vegetation that would be affected by construction. The company proposes prevention, mitigation, compensation and restoration measures, subject to the relevant approvals. The project is expected to consume approximately 8,000 cubic meters of water during construction and 1,500 cubic meters annually during operation, mainly for panel cleaning and sanitary services. Submitting the environmental impact statement is one step in the assessment process and does not, by itself, authorize construction. title: Engie secures financing for 300 MWh battery expansion in Australia - Energy Storage
content: Engie has announced the successful financial close for a major expansion of the Hazelwood battery energy storage system (BESS) built at the site of the retired Hazelwood coal-fired power station in the Australian state of Victoria. The milestone comes after Victorian Energy Minister Jaclyn Symes last week named Hazelwood BESS Line Co. Pty. Ltd. a “Declared Transmission System Operator,” allowing the project to use existing transmission infrastructure. As an established power generation site, Hazelwood has access to 1.6 GW of transmission capacity. The expansion will add a 150 MW/300 MWh BESS to the Hazelwood site, building on the existing 150 MW/150 MWh battery that was developed by Engie and storage specialist Eku Energy and has been operating since 2023 . Engie secured complete ownership of the Hazelwood BESS earlier this year, acquiring Eku Energy’s 30% stake. Symes said the project will increase the site’s total installed battery capacity to 300 MW/450 MWh, reinforcing Hazelwood’s role as a major source of flexible energy infrastructure for Victoria and the National Electricity Market (NEM). “The expansion of the Hazelwood Battery Energy Storage System is another important step in Victoria’s energy transition, helping to store more of our abundant clean, renewable energy,” she said. Laura Caspari, chief executive officer and managing director of renewables and batteries at Engie Australia , said the expansion is underpinned by strong customer demand for battery storage, driven by its ability to store low-cost solar generation during the day and dispatch it during periods of higher evening demand. “The Hazelwood battery has already demonstrated the value that energy storage can bring to the electricity system,” she said. “Expanding the facility allows us to build on that success while making use of existing infrastructure, enabling the continued growth of renewable energy across Victoria,” Chinese inverter and storage system manufacturer Sungrow has been tapped to supply the battery technology for the project, while Spanish infrastructure development group Elecnor will deliver the balance-of-plant and associated infrastructure works. Engie said key contracts have been executed, with construction commencing later this year and commercial operations targeted from 2028. The project is expected to generate up to 370 jobs during the construction phase. title: I bought a $199 Walmart e-bike, and what arrived shocked me
content:
I’ve tested e-bikes that cost $10,000. I’ve tested e-bikes that cost $500. But until recently, I’d never tested a brand-new e-bike that cost less than a nice set of bicycle tires.
So when I stumbled across a $199 e-bike for sale through Walmart’s website, my curiosity got the better of me.
To be clear, I wasn’t expecting it to be good. I wasn’t even really expecting it to be acceptable. This was more of a morbid curiosity experiment: What exactly does $199 buy you in the world of e-bikes?
Apparently, the answer is: more than I expected, but also fewer pedals than I expected.
The bike in question is from a brand called “Bropath”, and it’s a tiny folding e-bike with 14-inch wheels, a 350/500W rear hub motor (disparity based on which marketing blurb you read), and a surprisingly large 576Wh battery.
On paper, that’s actually fairly impressive, especially for the rock-bottom price. The bike claims a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h) and around 20 miles (32 km) of range. There’s a throttle, pedal assist, a suspension fork, mechanical disc brakes, a rear rack/basket that also houses the battery, and even a folding frame.
Things started getting interesting as soon as I pulled it out of the box, which you’ll definitely want to check out in my unboxing and testing video.
The bike was mostly assembled, but the battery basket wasn’t actually attached to the rack. There were holes where bolts clearly should have gone, but no bolts. I checked the box. I checked the packaging. I checked the instructions.
No bolts.
Eventually I resorted to temporarily ratchet-strapping the entire battery basket to the bike, which is not generally a step included in professional bicycle assembly.
Then, just as I thought I was ready for a test ride, I noticed another small problem: the bike didn’t have pedals.
Not “the pedals weren’t installed.” There simply weren’t any pedals in the box.
My guess is that an accessory box containing the pedals and battery mounting hardware was forgotten during packaging, or perhaps I received a re-packaged bike and they were left out. Fortunately, I live, eat, and breathe bikes, so my garage contains enough miscellaneous bicycle parts to make a small bike shop jealous. I eventually found two long bolts that fit the battery basket and a spare pair of pedals.
Before that, though, I did what any reasonable person would do: I rode it like a scooter with my feet resting on the bare cranks.
And that’s where things got surprising: the darn thing actually worked.
The little e-bike pulled away under throttle and moderately quickly got me cruising at nearly 20 mph (32 km/h). The brakes, which look like they were manufactured from approximately the same grade of metal as a soup can, actually stopped the bike reasonably well. The motor had decent power, the throttle worked, and once I installed pedals, the pedal assist worked too. On that note though: the single-speed design and small 14″ wheels meant that once the pedal assist kicked in, you’d quickly be going faster than your feet could keep up on the pedals. With that ghost pedaling in effect, the pedal assist quickly became useless, so don’t expect to ride this as a pedal-assist bike.
To test out the cargo capacity of the little battery basket, I took it on a shopping trip and managed to haul home several bags of groceries. I wouldn’t load it down with several cases of beer, but light duty grocery runs seems possible.
Is it a good e-bike? I wouldn’t go that far. But for $199, it was shockingly adequate. And I mean that as a compliment.
Yes, there are plenty of compromises. The suspension fork feels like a wet noodle, to the point that I’d probably rather have a rigid fork. The tiny 14-inch wheels combined with the cheap suspension make rough pavement and gravel paths fairly unpleasant. The seatpost is so short that even I can’t get a particularly good pedaling position, and I’m not exactly an NBA center.
And like I mentioned, the single-speed drivetrain also means that once the pedal assist gets you moving quickly, your legs can’t really keep up with the gearing. You wind up ghost pedaling while the motor does most of the work.
There are bigger questions, too.
I don’t know what cells are inside that 576Wh battery, and I certainly wouldn’t assume the battery has the sort of third-party safety certification I’d prefer to see on an e-bike. I don’t know how many years – or months – the suspension fork will last. I don’t know how the folding mechanism will hold up after hundreds of cycles, because it definitely doesn’t look robust.
And if something does break, you’re probably largely on your own. At this price, you’re not paying for a nationwide dealer network or a robust customer service department. This is basically a white-labeled budget e-bike, and part of the $199 experience is accepting that you will likely become your own mechanic.
That’s why I wouldn’t recommend this bike to most people.
If you can afford to spend more on a quality e-bike from an established company with better components, a certified battery, replacement parts, and real customer support, I think you should. When people ask me what the most affordable e-bike is that is still good quality, I generally send them to a $799 Lectric XP Lite-series e-bike. By the time you start upgrading parts on a bike like this $199 Walmart bike, adding likes better fork, brakes, drivetrain, or other components, you could have simply bought a better e-bike in the first place.
But there’s another side to this.
For someone who genuinely only has $200 to spend and needs transportation, this thing is transportation.
It got me to the store. It got me to lunch. It carried groceries. It cruised at nearly 20 mph. Once I supplied the missing parts myself, everything basically worked (and I assume most people will be luckier than me and get all the parts in the box).
And that’s what surprised me most.
Top comment by Mrvc
Good enough is better then nothing. It fills a gap. Most of China is riding around on sub $300 ebikes. Those folding bikes are getting very cheap I've seen them for around $50 fob. It's amazing they have brought the cost down for folding bikes so much 15 years ago they were several times more expensive then a regular bike. Now a folding ebike for less then the fancy brands and stores were trying to sell a folding bike. As long as a it last a few years and doesn't blow up it's a win for personal transportation.
I went into this experiment expecting a $199 e-bike to be almost comically terrible. Instead, I found something that was undeniably cheap, questionable in several places, and certainly not something I’d choose as my everyday e-bike – yet was also far more functional than it had any right to be at this price.
There’s a big difference between “good” and “good for $199.”
This bike definitely isn’t the former.
But somehow, against all odds, it might actually be the latter.

title: BYD launches new Seagull EV with 5-minute Flash Charging, starting under $10,000
content:
Peter Johnson
| Oct 20 2026 - 7:31 am PT
new Seagull EV is now its cheapest electric car in China with 5-minute Flash Charging, and starts at under $10,000.
BYD’s second-generation Seagull EV price and range
The all-electric hatchback is BYD’s smallest, most affordable EV in China. Sold as the Dolphin Surf and Dolphin Mini in Europe, the UK, and other global markets, the Seagull is among the world’s top-selling EVs.
For its second generation, BYD upgraded it with more interior space, its new Blade Battery 2.0 and 5-minute Flash Charging technology, and a few added premium extras.
The new Seagull EV is now on sale in China, starting at just 62,900 yuan, or about $9,500. That’s with BYD’s “Super Trade-in” promotion.
Regular prices start at 65,900 yuan ($9,900), which is still less than its predecessor. The first-gen Seagull EV normally cost 69,900 yuan ($10,500) without incentives.
BYD’s new Seagull EV is available in five variants, priced from 65,900 yuan to 99,900 yuan ($9,900 to $15,000), without a trade-in.
The second-generation Seagull is 425 mm longer and has a 150 mm longer wheelbase than its predecessor. It now measures 4,205 mm long, 1,810 mm wide, and 1,570 mm high, with a 2,650 mm wheelbase. It also gains another seat thanks to the added space, with room for five passengers.
Unlike the current model, which is front-wheel-drive, the new Seagull switches to rear-wheel-drive. The setup uses a more powerful 85 kW (114 hp) or 95 kW (127 hp) electric motor, up from the 55 kW (75 hp) that its predecessor offered.
BYD second-generation Seagull EV (Source: Zhang Zhuo)
To improve the ride quality and handling, BYD upgraded the rear suspension to a multi-link independent system.
Inside, BYD overhauled the interior with its latest in-car software and technology. The setup includes a larger 15.6″ center infotainment screen, a two-spoke steering wheel, a redesigned center console with smart storage, and added physical buttons.
BYD second-generation Seagull EV interior (Source: BYD)
All variants include the DiLink 150 smart cockpit and BYD’s 140 km/h high-speed tire blowout stability system.
Buyers can upgrade to the optional DiPilot 300 system with God’s Eye B intelligent driving assistance. The upgraded system uses a roof-mounted LiDAR to offer ADAS features, including City Navigation on Autopilot (CNOA) and smart parking.
The front seats now include heating, ventilation, and massage functions. BYD added a few other premium extras, including ambient lighting, a 50W wireless phone charger, and smart storage.
With BYD’s Flash Charging tech, the new battery can charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes. A full recharge, or 10% to 97%, takes just nine minutes. Even in temperatures as low as -30°C, it takes 12 minutes to charge from 20% to 97%.
The new Seagull EV is available with two BYD Blade 2.0 LFP battery packs: 30.1 kWh and 39.2 kWh, providing CLTC ranges of 320 km (199 miles) and 420 km (261 miles), respectively.
After launching in China, BYD is expected to introduce the larger, upgraded version overseas, likely as the second-generation Dolphin Surf and Dolphin Mini.

title: How electric school buses power 1,000 homes in California - and make money
content:
A fleet of 74 school buses have spent the last two years powering about a thousand homes, taking stress off the grid, thanks to V2G chargers built in America.
If you’ve spent much time around the electric vehicle space, you may have heard about vehicle-to-grid, perhaps by the acronym V2G (or its cousins, V2H/V2L/V2X, etc).
The basic idea is: if we’re looking to add batteries to the grid or to homes to increase stability and smooth out demand, why don’t we use the massive amounts of batteries available inside electric vehicles for that purpose?
The idea has been talked about for years, but for the most part has not reached wide adoption. The California Energy Commission estimates that V2H could save homeowners a few hundred dollars per summer, and cut peak demand by up to 5GW statewide if it was broadly implemented. But to do this with consumer EVs, homes would mostly need some sort of costly equipment added, and most EVs aren’t V2G-enabled (though that may be changing).
But for fleet EVs, installation can be a lot easier. Putting V2G in homes requires a lot of small scale projects, distributed across a region. But putting V2G in a fleet location lets you access a lot of batteries in one big project, and lets you aggregate those batteries more easily.
So that’s exactly what Tellus Power, a charging equipment manufacturer in Irvine, CA, is doing. We took a tour of its facility and met with CEO Mike Calise and CTO Srikanth Kanaparthi.
The company has been building AC and DC chargers (up to 480kW) since 2010, but its newest push is into V2G chargers, particularly for fleets. It assembles them in America, and they’re “Build America Buy America” compliant.
Its first project in this push was an installation of V2G chargers for Oakland, CA’s school district, covering 74 school buses. The chargers were built by Tellus, and the project is operated by Zum. We first wrote about the Oakland project in 2024, but now we have a couple years of data to show how it’s going.
Collectively, the buses have a total of 11.5MWh of energy storage. Buses fill up overnight, use about 20-40% of their charge during the day, then plug in to V2G chargers after the school day and discharge to feed the grid, just in time for the late afternoon rush on electricity, when people get home and turn on air conditioning, start cooking, turn on the lights and so on.
Or on holidays and summertime (when the grid is the most stressed in California), they can be a grid resource all day long.
74 buses may not sound like much, but with the amount of energy available on board and the total power output of the chargers, it can fuel a lot of houses. The fleet can discharge at about 2 Megawatts at once, and each house uses about 2 kilowatts on average in the evening (though that can spike higher due to HVAC/EV use). That means, altogether, this fleet of 74 buses can power around a thousand homes.
Over the course of the last two years, the bus fleet has returned a total of 1.7GWh of energy to the grid, and has had over 99.5% uptime. This basically turns the fleet into a small and reliable peaker plant, which has delivered on the order of hundreds of thousands of dollars worth of electricity to the grid over the last couple years.
Tellus says V2G capacity can get onto the grid faster than any other kind of power plant. A fleet V2G depot can take months to deploy, compared to a timeline of years to build and attach other power plants to the grid. And Tellus says that its chargers differ from others on the market in that they don’t require large transformers on-site, which makes deployment faster and less expensive.
V2G isn’t strictly a “power plant,” since it’s not generating electricity. But it does shift supply to when it’s needed most, which is also when it’s most expensive. This “energy arbitrage” lets Zum buy power when it’s cheap and sell it when it’s expensive, which makes money.
That’s Tellus’ oldest project, but there are others in place and being built – 4 school buses in Burlington, VT; 2 city bus chargers for Lynch Bus Lines in Burnaby, British Columbia, Canada; a pilot program at 3 school district sites for ComEd in Illinois; and a fleet of 104 school buses (scaling to 238) in San Francisco, CA.
Top comment by THT
Very nice!
It's only one school district. If it is most school districts in CA, like 100 school districts, it could be 200 MW of power, which definitely chips at reducing gas peaker plant usage.
If these busses had solar PV on top? It's ever chipping at reducing emissions. That's the great thing about solar+storage, you can incrementally add it, just a little at a time, and year by year, it becomes cheaper, more effective and will power more and more of our energy needs.
But even though buses are a popular choice for V2G, there are plenty of other municipal vehicles that are ripe for electrification, which have similar duty cycles and could be used for grid services.
Trash trucks are an obvious one, and they’re the next direction Tellus would like to go in. There are a number of electric garbage trucks out there, and they could generate revenue to offset costs in the same way that school buses can.
All of this together offers a large revenue opportunity for fleets, whether those fleets be private or public. If you have a bunch of vehicles, running those vehicles off of batteries can both save you money on fuel (especially with oil prices being at all-time highs) and generate revenue with grid services, if you install V2G chargers.

title: Polestar and Oxford wired up drivers to measure how performance feels
content:
Fred Lambert
| Oct 20 2026 - 6:06 am PT
Credit: Polestar
Polestar and the University of Oxford put 12 drivers in eye trackers and heart-rate monitors and sent them around a Swedish racetrack in two versions of the Polestar 4. The goal was to put numbers on something no spec sheet captures: how performance feels to the person driving.
The 544 hp Polestar 4 Dual motor with Performance pack delivered 32% higher peak acceleration than the 268 hp Rear motor version on matched laps, and it needed 15% less steering effort to do it. Drivers also rated it far higher on the experience.
How Oxford and Polestar tried to measure the “feel” of performance
The pilot study comes from researchers at the University of Oxford’s SDG Impact Lab, working with Polestar. It took place at the Gotland Ring, a track built inside an old limestone quarry on the Swedish island of Gotland.
Credit: Polestar
Each participant drove both cars in calm and dynamic conditions:
Polestar 4 Rear motor:
200 kW (268 hp)
Polestar 4 Dual motor with Performance pack:
400 kW (544 hp)
The researchers logged vehicle telemetry alongside heart-rate data, eye tracking and psychological assessments, then interviewed the drivers afterward. The idea is to line up what the car was doing at a given moment with what was happening to the human inside it.
Credit: Polestar
Photos from the test also show drivers wearing electrode caps, though brain activity isn’t among the measures Polestar published results for.
Several of those measures reacted when the driving got more intense. In dynamic driving, participants blinked less, their pupils got bigger, and they held their gaze longer on a given point. Researchers read that as deeper attention. They could also tie moments in the telemetry to changes in the drivers’ physiological activation.
32% more acceleration, 15% less steering effort
The car-to-car comparison is the most concrete part of the study. On matched fast laps, where both versions were driven at virtually the same pace, the Performance pack car hit 32% higher peak acceleration while requiring 15% less steering effort. It also pulled bigger cornering loads and logged more hard-acceleration events.
That steering figure is the one I’d focus on. You’d expect twice the power to mean more work for the driver at the same lap time. Instead, the dual-motor car asked less of them.
Credit: Polestar
The drivers’ own scores moved in the same direction. On the study’s Performance/Dynamics scale, the Performance version scored 89.2 out of 100, versus 67.7 for the Rear motor. Overall experiential quality came in at 93.0 versus 77.9, with most drivers rating the Performance version higher on both.
“A controlled roller coaster”
The interviews are where it gets more human. Drivers didn’t describe performance as pure adrenaline. They talked about a mix of physical arousal, trust in the car, a sense of control, and intense focus. Several of them, independently, landed on the same image: a “controlled roller coaster.”
One participant said the car “makes you feel like a better driver than you are.” Researchers found drivers linked that combination of thrill, trust and control more consistently to the Performance version.
Max Klapow, a doctoral researcher at the Oxford SDG Impact Lab, framed it this way:
“Performance is not simply about going faster. It is about giving the driver a sense of confidence and control through predictable vehicle responses.”
Christian Samson, Polestar’s head of product attributes, said the company wanted to understand “something that can’t be captured by a specification sheet alone.”
Now, the caveats. The researchers themselves call this a feasibility pilot and say a larger study is needed to establish whether the findings are reliable and valid. It’s 12 people, Polestar’s own cars, and Polestar is attaching a documentary series to it.
There’s also an awkward backdrop for US readers. As we reported in June,
Polestar was barred from selling new cars in the US
starting with the 2027 model year under the connected vehicle rule, even though the Polestar 4 is built in South Korea. The brand is now centering its plans on Europe, with the
Formula 2030 concept previewing its next models
Credit: Polestar
Electrek’s Take
This is a topic that has fascinated me for years. I’ve driven a lot of EVs, and the spec sheet tells me very little about whether I’ll enjoy one. Two cars with the same 0-60 mph time can feel completely different. One makes you grin. The other pins you to the seat and leaves you oddly numb.
The problem is that it’s genuinely hard to discuss. What feels like confidence to one driver feels like an overassisted steering rack to another. It’s different for everyone, and there’s basically no quantitative data on it, so the conversation ends up being reviewers, me included, trading adjectives.
So kudos to Polestar and Oxford for trying. Matching blink rate, pupil size and heart rate against steering effort and telemetry is a real attempt to connect the engineering to the experience, and I haven’t seen an automaker publish anything like it.
And it matters more now than ever. EVs turned acceleration into a commodity. Family crossovers do 0-60 mph in under 5 seconds. If everyone has the straight-line numbers, the difference comes down to how the car makes you feel, and right now most automakers are tuning that by gut.
I wouldn’t take 89.2 versus 67.7 to the bank. Twelve drivers isn’t a big sample, and nobody needed a study to tell them a 544 hp car is on average more fun than a 268 hp one. But the steering result and that “better driver than you are” quote get at what I think separates great performance cars from fast ones: they make you feel in control while you go faster.
What I’d love to see next is the bigger version with cars from different brands. Would a Model 3 Performance, an Ioniq 5 N and a Polestar 4 produce measurably different responses at the same lap times? That’s the study I want to read.

title: 辽宁、河北两大固态电池项目落地
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，固态电池产业化项目持续推进。百度参与的0.5GW固态电芯项目拟落地大连，阳光新能源半固态电池产业园则签约落地邢台，两个项目均计划于2027年推进建设或试产。
百度参与，0.5GW固态电芯项目拟落地
10月13日，快界集团与大连中英产业园开发有限公司、天津城建集团有限公司及百度相关负责人举行交流，围绕轻型电动车固态快充项目探讨合作。
各方初步达成共识，计划在大连建设首期0.5GW固态电芯产线及固态电池PACK项目，中期推进上下游产业链建设。该产线计划于2027年上半年启动建设。
百度是一家以人工智能为核心业务的科技公司，旗下萝卜快跑是全球主要的无人驾驶出行服务平台之一，业务已覆盖全球28座城市，累计自动驾驶里程超过3.5亿公里。
快界集团全称为浙江快界科技集团，是一家深耕电池制造与新能源技术领域的高新技术企业。集团聚焦新一代固态锂离子电池攻关，着力解决传统液态锂电池在能量密度、安全性等方面的痛点，推动电池技术向高能量、高安全、长寿命方向迭代升级。
阳光新能源半固态电池产业园落地
10月15日，河北邢台市委、市政府与阳光新能源开发股份有限公司举行工作会谈。阳光新能源已与邢台市经开区完成签约，计划建设光学镜头及半固态电池产业园，项目即将开工建设。公司董事长张许成表示，将确保2027年一季度实现设备进场调试和试生产。
阳光新能源业务涉及光伏、风电、储能、充电及风光储氢充多能融合等领域。阳光电源2026年半年报显示，阳光新能源是公司新能源投资开发业务的实施主体，业务覆盖国内30多个省、自治区和直辖市，海外市场涉及17个国家和地区，全球累计开发建设光伏电站、风电场规模超过6100万千瓦。
除邢台半固态电池产业园外，阳光新能源近期也在推进储能项目建设。今年9月，其签约广西梧州蒙山县300MW/600MWh新型储能电站项目，总投资约9亿元，采用磷酸铁锂电池技术，预计2027年7月建成并网。
此外，阳光电源于今年8月在埃及苏伊士运河经济区泰达产业园启动储能制造基地建设，项目总投资5000万美元，规划年产能最高达10GWh，预计2027年4月投产。

title: 超48GWh！湖南裕能/中科海钠等7企披露电池及储能项目进展
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，湖南裕能、广浩能源、中科海钠、海容科技、亿昇达等企业相继披露电池及储能相关项目进展，涉及磷酸铁锂、钠离子电池、负极材料、全固态电池及储能PACK等领域。
湖南裕能拟投资20亿元建设磷酸铁锂项目
10月19日，湖南裕能召开董事会会议，审议通过投资建设湖南裕能六期磷酸铁锂项目的议案，计划投资不超过20亿元。
据公告，该项目选址于湖南省湘潭市雨湖区鹤岭镇，建设期为12个月，总建筑面积约8万平方米，主要建设生产厂房及相关配套设施，并购置磷酸铁锂成套生产线设备。项目资金来源为企业自筹。
湖南裕能表示，此次投资旨在进一步完善公司磷酸铁锂产能布局，提升核心产品供给能力，以满足新能源汽车、储能及新兴应用领域未来业务发展和市场拓展需求。
广浩能源35GWh储能项目落地河南
10月15日，广浩能源与河南省兰考县人民政府举行储能项目投资协议签约仪式。
根据协议，本次签约项目包括20GWh石墨烯复合钠离子储能系统及15GWh集装箱式储能系统，总投资约120亿元，总占地面积近千亩，建设周期为12个月。
中科海钠签约10GWh钠离子电池项目
10月14日，中科海钠（武汉）科技有限责任公司与武汉市江夏区签约建设10GWh钠离子电池生产线项目。
据悉，该项目一期规划建设3GWh钠离子电池电芯产线，企业称其为当前全球最大钠离子电池电芯产线。项目计划于2027年初启动建设，并于2027年内实现投产。
海容科技8万吨负极材料项目签约
10月14日，乌兰浩特市人民政府与湖北海容科技有限公司就“新能源＋8万吨负极材料生产项目”举行签约仪式。该项目总投资21亿元，拟选址于内蒙古兴安盟经济技术开发区，计划于2027年5月开工建设。
企查查显示，海容科技成立于2022年11月，主要从事新能源电池及储能器件负极材料的研发、生产与销售，注册资本约3240.74万元。公司由深圳俊领新能源科技有限公司、Sanode International Co.,Limited等5家企业共同持有。
亿昇达绍兴0.5GWh全固态电池生产线投产
10月13日，杭州亿昇达新能源科技有限公司绍兴工厂投产，其0.5GWh大圆柱全固态电池生产线正式投产。
据悉，投产仪式现场，亿昇达与核心客户签订首批500万只大圆柱电芯战略框架协议，产品计划应用于煤矿等特种装备领域。
国天智充储能PACK项目计划年内投产
近日，国天智慧储能模组PACK集装箱生产线项目在内蒙古二连浩特市中蒙经济合作区加快建设。项目由二连浩特市国天智充新能源科技有限公司投资建设，总投资约4000万元，今年8月开工，计划于10月20日前后进场安装设备，力争年内投产。
据悉，该项目建设内容包括一座5103平方米的生产厂房和一座1071平方米的库房。目前，厂房主体工程基本完工，正在进行封顶施工。项目生产线涵盖电芯处理、模组装配、激光焊接、PACK集成及系统测试五大工段，主要生产集装箱式储能单元，产品面向新能源储能电站、工商业及交通电动化等应用场景。
3GWh储能PACK项目进入调试阶段
近日，茂县安诚新能源有限公司3GWh储能PACK高端装备制造项目两条生产线已完成设备安装，进入设备调试阶段。
据悉，该项目总投资2.88亿元，主要购置安装新型储能系统智能化生产设备，新建3GWh新型储能高端装备生产线。

title: 远信储能通过港交所上市聆讯
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，10月19日，远信储能通过香港联合交易所上市聆讯，拟在港交所主板上市，招银国际担任独家保荐人。
回顾上市进程，远信储能于2026年1月9日首次向港交所递交上市申请，后因申请文件有效期届满而失效；8月9日，公司再次递交上市申请。
此前，远信储能已于7月获得中国证监会境外发行上市备案通知书，拟发行不超过1.35亿股境外上市普通股，并涉及13名股东合计3.52亿股境内未上市股份转为境外上市股份。
营收方面，2023—2025年，远信储能分别实现收入4.35亿元、11.44亿元和18.68亿元；同期毛利分别为9382.6万元、2.04亿元和3.01亿元。2026年前四个月，公司实现收入2.80亿元，上年同期为846.9万元；毛利达到7658.5万元，毛利率由上年同期的-10.9%提升至27.4%。
2026年1—4月，公司实现营业收入2.80亿元，净利润约0.23亿元，同比由亏转盈。
近年来，远信储能持续向大型储能系统解决方案转型。2023—2025年，公司大型储能系统解决方案收入分别为720万元、4.77亿元和16.69亿元，占总收入的比例由1.6%提升至41.7%和89.4%。2026年前四个月，大型储能系统解决方案收入为2.14亿元，占同期总收入76.4%，毛利为5260万元，毛利率为24.6%。
2026年1—4月，公司大型储能系统解决方案收入为2.14亿元，占同期总营收的76.4%，销量为271.4MWh。公司披露，期内完成5个大型储能项目部署，包括匈牙利欧罗什拉尼110MWh项目。
同时，远信储能加快海外市场拓展。2025年，远信储能海外收入为880万元，其中主要来自美国及西班牙；2026年1—4月，海外收入进一步增加，约占同期总营收的44.6%。同期，公司海外大型及工商业储能系统解决方案的平均售价高于国内市场。
目前，远信储能拥有镇江、姚安、大理及嘉兴4家储能系统产品及部件生产工厂。其中，镇江、姚安和大理工厂已投入商业运营，嘉兴工厂处于试运营阶段。2025年，前三家工厂总产能为6.8GWh。
公司计划推进乌镇工厂建设，预计于2028年5月投产，设计产能约10GWh；朝阳和金昌两座工厂的开发则暂时延后。

title: 注册资本10亿，宁德时代、奇瑞再设芜湖电池新公司
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，10月19日，宁德时代与奇瑞汽车的第二家合资公司——宁德时代奇瑞（芜湖）新能源科技有限公司完成注册设立，注册资本10亿元。
企查查信息显示，此次新公司选址安徽芜湖市南陵县，业务范围包含电池制造与销售、电池零配件生产与销售、储能技术服务等。
股权结构上，宁德时代合计持股51%，其中包含1.4553%的间接持股；奇瑞汽车持股49%。
图：新公司工商信息
此前，2026年2月13日，宁德时代与奇瑞已成立时代奇瑞（合肥）新能源科技有限公司。该公司注册资本20亿元，注册选址合肥巢湖，同样由宁德时代持股51%，奇瑞汽车、奇瑞商用车持股42.33%、6.67%。
梳理双方的合作时间线，宁德时代与奇瑞集团的合作开始于2022年12月。2022年12月，宁德时代与奇瑞控股集团签署战略合作框架协议，启动全面合作。
2023年4月，双方联合推出电池品牌ENER-Q，并官宣钠离子电池首发搭载奇瑞车型，共同开展多材料体系电池产品合作开发。
2026年2月，双方首家电芯合资主体时代奇瑞（合肥）新能源科技有限公司完成注册。2026年10月，第二家合资企业宁德时代奇瑞（芜湖）新能源科技有限公司成立。
从业务范围来看，两家合资公司的经营方向相近，均以动力电池、电池零部件的生产制造为主，同时覆盖储能相关技术等业务。截至目前，两家合资公司的产能规划、项目投产时间等细节，暂未对外披露。

title: 协鑫科技拟25亿收购协鑫锂电约81%股权
content:
10月19日，协鑫科技发布公告，宣布与协鑫集团订立谅解备忘录，拟收购四川协鑫锂电科技有限公司约81.91%的股权，收购金额约人民币25亿元（约29.36亿港元）。
据了解，四川协鑫锂电位于四川眉山仁寿县经济开发区，主要从事新能源电池用磷酸铁锂正极材料的研发、生产与销售，公司一期规划磷酸铁锂年产能达12万吨。
此前协鑫科技主营业务为多晶硅及硅片产品，受硅料价格持续低迷拖累，2026年上半年净利润亏损20.81亿元。而在今年5月，协鑫科技确立了"硅锂碳同构"战略，旗下乐山鑫能20万吨磷酸铁锂项目于6月投产并实现盈利。协鑫科技在公告中表示，本次收购有助于公司拓展至受国家碳中和政策支持的磷酸铁锂正极材料领域，降低对多晶硅及硅片产品价格周期的依赖，提升盈利稳定性，并利用目标公司的研发能力、生产设施及客户网络打造新的增长动力。本次收购完成后，四川协鑫锂电将成为协鑫科技的非全资附属公司并纳入合并报表，进一步增厚正极材料产能与营收规模。
协鑫集团在公告中对协鑫锂电作出业绩承诺，预计2027年及2028年合计经调整净利润不低于6.2亿元，并于2028年底前开发出压实密度在2.8g/cm³以上的第6代磷酸铁锂正极材料产品。若未达标，卖方需从交易对价中向协鑫科技支付补偿。

title: This Chinese EV Is Now Made In Europe. More Are Coming
content:
Stellantis is building Leapmotor’s B10 electric crossover in Spain, with a second model ready to join it next year.
Photo by:
Leapmotor
10:16am ET
Leapmotor has started building the B10 in Spain, with the B05 expected to follow in early 2027.
Leapmotor previously assembled the T03 in Poland using Chinese kits, but production ended in March 2025.
Chinese brands are expanding European production through local partners, existing factories and new plants.
Chinese automakers don’t necessarily need to build factories to start making cars in Europe. Sometimes, a European manufacturer already has the space and is happy to help. That’s what’s happening in Spain, where Stellantis has started building the Leapmotor B10 electric crossover and is preparing to add another model.
The companies officially started B10 production at Stellantis’ Zaragoza plant on October 16. This fulfills
Leapmotor’s Spanish production plans
announced earlier this year, giving the Chinese brand a manufacturing base in a major overseas market and, by extension, the entire European Union. Stellantis says it chose the facility for its available capacity, manufacturing expertise and quality.
Next to start production in Zaragoza is the B05 electric hatchback. Leapmotor confirmed its production allocation yesterday but without specifying a start date. Spanish news agency EFE reports the launch in the first quarter of 2027.
Leapmotor B05
Photo by: Leapmotor
This isn’t Leapmotor’s first attempt at European production.
The tiny T03
, which surprised us with its value and driving manners, was previously assembled at Stellantis’ Tychy factory in Poland. That operation started in 2024, using semi-knocked-down kits shipped from China.
Stellantis controls 51% of its joint venture with Leapmotor, giving it rights to manufacture and sell its vehicles outside China.
The Polish T03 experiment
was short-lived, though, and Stellantis ended T03 assembly on March 30, 2025, without explaining why.
Leapmotor is far from the only Chinese automaker looking to establish a manufacturing presence in Europe.
BYD is building its own massive factory in Hungary
Xpeng turned to contract manufacturer Magna
in Austria.
GAC followed Xpeng’s lead
, bringing new work to a facility that previously assembled the Fisker Ocean.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
Existing factories can also offer a route back into production after their previous occupants leave. Chery partnered with Ebro to use
Nissan’s former Barcelona plant
. Audi’s shuttered Brussels factory illustrates why those possibilities shouldn’t be mistaken for completed deals, though.
Nio reportedly wanted to take it over
, although its CEO denied the plans, and in September a property company was announced as the buyer.
For European automakers, Chinese expansion now presents an awkward choice: compete with these brands, build their cars, or do both. Stellantis has chosen the third option. At Zaragoza, a Chinese competitor’s growth is also keeping the factory lights on.

title: GM Is Closing Its Detroit EV Battery Plant
content:
The facility used to make batteries for the Cadillac Celestiq luxury sedan, as well as drive units for the Chevy Corvette E-Ray.
Photo by:
General Motors
8:29am ET
GM's Brownstown Battery Assembly plant will be closed.
The facility used to manufacture batteries and drive units for the Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray, as well as battery packs for the Cadillac Celestiq.
The move is part of GM's bigger shift in manufacturing, where it is now prioritizing gas vehicles,
General Motors
is shutting down its 480,000-square-foot battery assembly plant in Detroit, which used to supply high-voltage batteries for the
Cadillac Celestiq EV
and the Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray, as well as drive units for Chevy’s electrified two-door sports car.
The Brownstown Battery Assembly facility, which was opened in 2009, will be decommissioned by next summer when the lease ends, according to
Automotive News
, quoting a person familiar with the situation. General Motors confirmed the closure for InsideEVs, adding that the factory's activity will be moved to other facilities. "The lease on the Brownstown Battery Assembly plant is ending next year, and GM is planning to transition this work to other nearby GM facilities," a company spokesperson told InsideEVs.
The exclusive and very expensive Cadillac Celestiq used to get its high-voltage batteries from Brownstown.
Photo by: Cadillac
The move comes as the American automaker continues to absorb billions of dollars in losses associated with the shift in its powertrain strategy. While the company continues to build EVs, its attention has shifted to making more gas-powered vehicles. Earlier this year,
GM exited a battery factory joint venture with Samsung SDI
, leaving the Korean company in full control of the upcoming facility in Indiana. In 2024, the automaker pulled out of a $2.5 billion battery plant in Lansing, Michigan, leaving LG Energy Solution at the helm.
The Detroit factory’s employee count went from around 300 at its peak to less than a dozen when the company reduced output due to weaker-than-expected demand. Affected workers were notified earlier this year and have been offered jobs at other facilities in the area.
In addition to the battery plant closure, General Motors is also looking to give its shuttered hydrogen fuel cell facility in Detroit a new lease on life. Initially, the plant was destined to develop a new fuel cell system that would have eventually powered at least two vehicles—one from GM and one from Honda—but
the deal went belly up
because there was no clear path to profitability.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
However, when the partnership was still standing, GM shook hands with Piston Automotive, which involved a $55 million investment, 150 new jobs, and a 300,000 sq ft facility. GM recently took over the long-term lease of the building from Piston, according to
Automotive News
. GM said it is evaluating other uses for the site, but it has not made any decisions.
After the $7,500 federal tax credit went away last year, the entire automotive industry had to reconsider its choices, and GM was hit extremely hard. During the third quarter, the American company
sold 25,472 EVs stateside
, a steep drop compared to the 66,501 units shipped during the same period last year. Granted, last year’s Q3 included the massive wave of buyers who wanted to take advantage of the now-canceled tax credit, but the automaker’s numbers never recovered.

title: The 2027 Lexus NX Plug-In Hybrid Gets A Bigger Battery And Fast Charging
content:
The 2027 Lexus NX Plug-In Hybrid Gets A Bigger Battery And Fast Charging
Lexus axed the gas-only NX, leaving only the hybrid and plug-in hybrid versions.
- The 2027 Lexus NX is available with electrified powertrains exclusively.
- On the NX 450+ plug-in hybrid, the battery gets a capacity bump and fast charging through a native NACS port.
- More power and a longer all-electric range are also on the list of improvements.
The Lexus NX compact crossover is getting a makeover for 2027. The gas-only version has been scrapped from the lineup, leaving just the hybrid and plug-in hybrid powertrains on the table—and both get improvements.
A larger-capacity high-voltage battery enables a longer all-electric driving range on the 2027 Lexus NX 450h+ plug-in hybrid. What’s more, a native Tesla-style NACS charging port can now handle DC fast charging, significantly slashing waiting times.
The 2027 Lexus NX 450h+ gets DC fast-charging capabilities for the first time. In North America, it will come with a NACS charging port.
The plug-in crossover gets a 22.7-kilowatt-hour battery pack, up from the outgoing model’s 18.1 kWh, enabling a manufacturer-estimated 45 miles of range on electricity. That’s eight miles more than the previous model.
When it comes to charging, Lexus said the new NX 450h+ can go from 10% to 80% in 35 minutes when hooked to a 50-kilowatt DC fast charger. On AC charging, using a 6.6 kW 240-volt charger, the crossover needs two and a half hours to go from 10% to 100% state of charge.
Power is also up compared to the previous model. The NX 450h+ PHEV comes standard with electric all-wheel drive and delivers a combined system output of 324 horsepower, up from 304 hp in the 2026 model. The gain in power is mainly attributed to the front motor-generator, which now makes 203 hp instead of 180 hp. Meanwhile, the 2.5-liter gas engine delivers 186 hp, and the rear-axle electric motor is good for 54 hp.
According to Lexus, the new NX plug-in hybrid can accelerate from zero to 60 miles per hour in 5.7 seconds and on to a top speed of 124 mph.
The 2027 Lexus NX 350h hybrid also gets a small power bump, reaching a combined output of 244 hp, 4 hp more than before. Weirdly enough, this figure applies to both the front- and all-wheel-drive versions, though the AWD hybrid model can accelerate slightly quicker than its FWD brother, with a 0-60 mph time of 6.7 seconds, compared to the front-powered model’s 6.9 seconds.
The hybrid model’s front motor-generator makes 160 hp, with an additional 54 hp coming from the rear motor on the AWD version. Lexus said it redesigned the hybrid system to rely more on the electric motor-generators and deliver a more torque-rich feel. That said, the 1.1 kWh battery is unchanged from the previous model.
Under the skin, the 2027 NX’s suspension and steering have been revised, and the chassis rigidity has been improved, which should lead to a better driving experience, Lexus said.
Styling-wise, the compact crossover now comes with a new face, redesigned taillights, and black accents instead of chrome. Inside, all NX versions feature a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster and a 14-inch central infotainment screen running Lexus’ latest software.
The steering wheel has a slightly smaller diameter than the 2026 model. On the dash, a soft-touch horizontal control panel hides a set of responsive switches with translucent surface panels for temperature control, defroster, and defogger.
Last year’s base trim is out of the picture, leaving the Premium, Premium+, F SPORT, and Luxury grades on offer. All trim levels come standard with the automaker’s LSS+ 4.0 driver assistance system, which includes dynamic radar cruise control, lane centering, traffic jam assist, lane change assist, and automatic high beams.
Pricing for the 2027 Lexus NX has not been disclosed yet. The NX 350h hybrid is assembled at the Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada (TMMC) plant in Ontario, Canada, as well as the Toyota Motor Kyushu (TMK) plant in Japan. Meanwhile, the 2027 Lexus NX 450h+ plug-in hybrid is assembled only at the Toyota Motor Kyushu (TMK) factory.

title: Kia EV3 Lease Deals Are Here, And It’s Cheaper Than The Chevy Bolt And Nissan Leaf
content:
Kia’s new entry-level EV is coming for the competition.
Photo by:
4:28am ET
The Kia EV3 can now be leased or financed.
On a 36-month lease, Kia’s new entry-level EV is more affordable than its competitors.
For less than $400/month, customers can get an all-wheel-drive model.
has big expectations for the
crossover in the United States, and it’s doing everything it can to lure in buyers. After debuting in August with a $31,385 starting price, the entry-level electric hatchback is now coming after its biggest competitors with some aggressive lease and finance offers.
According to Kia, the base-spec 2027 EV3 Wind with a front-wheel-drive powertrain can be had for $321/month with a $3,999 down payment, a 36-month term, and a 10,000-mile yearly limit.
2027 Kia EV3 lease and finance offers
Photo by: Kia
The bog-standard
comes with a single, front-mounted electric motor that makes 201 horsepower. A 58.3-kilowatt-hour battery pack enables an EPA-estimated range of 221 miles. That’s more than decent, but Kia has an ace up its sleeve.
For just $8 more each month, customers can get behind the wheel of a 2027 EV3 Wind front-wheel drive, which gets a larger-capacity 81.4 kWh battery and a significantly longer driving range of 321 miles. The EV3 is also available with dual-motor all-wheel drive, and Kia wants $379/month for 36 months to lease you one in the same mid-spec Wind that offers heated front seats, a wireless phone charger, and wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity.
What’s more, Kia is putting $1,500 on the hood for new EV3 purchases, and customers who prefer financing get 0.9% APR for 48 months.
Gallery: 2027 Kia EV3 First Drive
With numbers like these, the EV3 is the second-most affordable EV to lease in Kia’s American lineup, after the discontinued Niro EV but before the larger EV6. More importantly, though, the EV3’s debut on the lease market undercuts the
Chevrolet Bolt
Nissan Leaf
With the same contract length and down payment, the base 2027 Chevy Bolt costs $423/month to lease, while the 2027 Nissan Leaf S+ can be had for $474/month. Nissan currently has a slightly better deal for the SV+ trim, though, at $449/month.
With these prices, the Bolt and Leaf, both of which are only available with front-wheel drive, are more expensive than the all-wheel-drive EV3. Range-wise, the longest-range Nissan Leaf delivers 303 miles on a full charge, while the Chevrolet Bolt manages 262 miles.
When buying with cash, the 2027 Chevy Bolt is still the cheapest, with a starting price of $28,995, but the Kia EV3 is not too far behind. With the $1,500 bonus, Kia’s new EV starts at $29,885. Meanwhile, the Nissan Leaf starts at $31,565.
The Kia EV3 took its sweet time getting here, but it’s finally here to capture an audience that its competitors have so far failed to attract. Sales of the Leaf and Bolt have been lackluster, to say the least, leaving plenty of room for the EV3 to swoop in. Kia said
it expects the EV3 to be its best-selling electric model in the U.S.
, but we’ll have to wait and see if Americans actually want a small battery-powered commuter car in their driveways.

title: Here's What It's Like To Take Delivery Of A Rivian R2
content:
You might be dreaming of what it's like to take delivery of an R2, but this is what it's like.
Photo by:
4:42pm ET
Taking delivery of a brand-new car is always an exciting moment. Getting your brand
Rivian R2
dropped off at home is even more exciting, because this thing is crucial to Rivian's future and an important model for America's struggling EV industry. But a new EV like the R2 can come with a steep learning curve, given its extraordinary levels of tech. In this new video from
State of Charge
, host Tom Moloughney takes delivery of his new R2 and shows you what it's like, and how the delivery specialist educates the customer.
After getting the boring paperwork out of the way, the specialist will give you a walkaround of the car, going over the color, interior, and wheel options you chose and all that fun stuff. But they also go over how some of the functions work, like the frunk and the keyfob (the R2 mercifully has a keyfob and not only stupid keycards, like
and Lucid). Do most customers need to know how to use every feature? No, probably not. But, hey, it's nice to have the educational option for those who need it.
Since Moloughney lives in New Jersey (as all wise people do), Rivian threw in a few goodies gratis, since NJ is a CARB state. So in the trunk of his new R2 was a J1772 adapter, a combo CCS1 adapter, and a portable charger, all on the house.
Photo by: Rivian
Moloughney says the specialist also went over some important info that even some seasoned EV owners might be curious about, like how the 120-volt socket in the trunk can deliver 16 amps, and the cool power sliding rear window.
Where most customers are going to at least need a crash course is inside. The R2 is chock full o' tech, like the Haptic Halo Wheels that control features on the steering wheel.
There are plenty of other teaching points in an R2's delivery process, so it's worth checking out. If you want to buy an R2 and are looking forward to what delivery day might be like, this could be a fun watch. Or if you're nervous about the R2's tech, and it's making you apprehensive about buying one, this video could help you see what the learning curve is actually like. Or maybe you just like hearing a Jersey guy talk EVs, which explains why you made it this far.

title: Used EVs Hit A Record Share Of Overall Used Car Sales In September
content:
Used EVs Hit A Record Share Of Overall Used Car Sales In September
Booming used EV sales suggest people do want plug-in models, as long as the price is right.
- Used electric cars reached a record 3.3% share of the total used car market.
- The Tesla Model Y, Chevy Equinox EV, and Nissan Ariya are some of the most popular used EVs.
- Prices of pre-owned models have increased due to higher demand.
Electric vehicles may be having a rough year in the new car market, but the demand for used models is soaring. Used EVs accounted for a record share of all used vehicle sales in the U.S. in September, as lower prices relative to brand new cars and a growing pool of pre-owned models returning to dealer lots helped drive demand.
A record 47,862 used EVs changed hands last month, up 12.3% from August and 21.2% from a year earlier, according to Cox Automotive’s latest EV Market Monitor. It’s a glimmer of hope after the end of federal tax credits last September and the recent rollback of fuel economy norms that hamstrung the sales of new EVs.
It also captures the broader affordability crisis in the auto industry. Not everyone can spend on a new electric car, whose average transaction price was $55,842 in September, according to Cox. Although more affordable models are now on sale, like the Chevy Bolt, Nissan Leaf, and the Kia EV3. However, sales of both the Bolt and Leaf have been lackluster. Chevy sold 3,866 Bolts in Q3, whereas Nissan only sold 634 Leafs, per Cox.
Nissan Ariya
However, the influx of used models is now making EV ownership possible for a broader group of buyers. Many of these models are larger and more practical crossovers like the Tesla Model Y and Chevy Equinox EV that U.S. buyers gravitate towards more than smaller models. This supply of incoming trade-ins and off-lease vehicles is giving shoppers more models and price points to choose from, per Cox.
The affordability equation is improving, albeit gradually, Cox said. The average listed price of a used EV fell 1.8% from August to $36,767 in September. That was still 6.2%, or $2,137, more than the average gas car. But the gap narrowed from $2,692 a month earlier, bringing used EVs closer to price parity with their combustion counterparts.
Tesla continued to lead the used EV market, while Ford and Chevy also posted strong gains. Used sales rose 21.3% for Chevy and 17.1% for Ford month over month. Among individual models, the Nissan Ariya and Chevy Equinox EV saw sales jump 42.5% and 41.9%, respectively. The Chevy Blazer EV, Ford Mustang Mach-E, Kia EV9, and Tesla Model Y also had strong demand among used EVs.
Chevy Equinox EV LT
Another encouraging sign was how much time used models were sitting on dealer lots. Used EV supply fell to 35 days in September, down 16.7% from August. The comparable figure for gas and other non-EVs was 46 days, suggesting used EVs were moving relatively quickly through the market.
That said, the contrast with new EVs is pretty striking. New EV sales fell 40.7% year over year in September to an estimated 86,632 units, although their share of new-car sales edged up to 6.5% as the broader market contracted.
The report added that the used market isn't big enough to offset that decline on its own, and EVs still carry a price premium. But a record market share suggests more shoppers are finding electric cars worth considering when they don't have to spend a fortune on them.

| Quelle:

Promotion von Stefan Resch: Intelligente Orthese erfasst Gangparameter und Belastungsdaten während des Gehens und gibt Nutzenden Feedback - Kombination aus technischer Entwicklung und Methoden der Mensch-Computer-Interaktion
Menschen mit Fußverletzungen oder eingeschränkter Fußfunktion sind häufig auf orthopädische Hilfsmittel, beispielsweise eine Sprunggelenk-Orthese, angewiesen. Gleichzeitig fehlen ihnen Möglichkeiten zu kontrollieren, welchen Belastungen ihr Fuß beim Gehen ausgesetzt ist – ein Aspekt, der auch Menschen mit Polyneuropathie an den Füßen, beispielsweise infolge von Diabetes, betrifft.
Wie smarte Geräte hier unterstützen können, hat Dr. Stefan Resch von der Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences (Frankfurt UAS) im Rahmen seiner Promotion untersucht.¹
Im Mittelpunkt seiner Arbeit stand die Entwicklung einer sensorisierten Fußorthese – quasi eine Einlegesohle mit integrierter Sensorik, die Gangparameter und Belastungsdaten während des Gehens erfassen und anhand dessen Feedback geben kann. Dabei kombinierte Resch die technische Entwicklung mit Methoden der Mensch-Computer-Interaktion.
Sein Ziel: besser zu verstehen, wie Menschen mit solchen Technologien interagieren und sie wahrnehmen. Ein Großteil seiner Arbeit fand dazu im Mixed-Reality-Labor der Frankfurt UAS statt.
Feedback durch Vibrationssignal
Im ersten Schritt entwickelte Resch eine smarte Einlegesohle für eine Fußorthese mit integrierter Sensorik und Feedbackfunktionen. Er vernetzte sie mit einer Gehhilfe, in deren Griff ebenfalls Sensoren und Vibrationsmodule integriert sind. Bei Überlastung erhält die betreffende Person ein Vibrationssignal – direkt über die Orthese oder über den Griff der Gehhilfe.
Auch eine Smartphone-App zur mobilen Erfassung der Daten gehörte zu Reschs Arbeit: Sie ermöglicht Nutzenden unter anderem die farbige Visualisierung des Fußsohlendrucks anhand einer Heatmap und bietet ein Gehtagebuch, das Gangdaten dokumentiert und den individuellen Schmerzlevel bewertet.
Virtual Reality für immersive Trainingsanwendungen
Im zweiten Forschungsschwerpunkt erprobte Resch die von ihm entwickelten Geräte mit Probanden. Er untersuchte, wie sich Virtual- und Mixed-Reality-Technologien nutzen lassen, um die Interaktion seiner smarten Geräte zwischen Patient*in und Gerät und deren Feedbackfunktionen in kontrollierten, immersiven Trainingsumgebungen zu evaluieren.
In der ersten Studie ging Resch der Frage nach, wie ein Mixed-Reality-Avatar, also ein digitaler Assistent, Nutzende beim Onboarding der Smartphone-App unterstützen kann. Die Ergebnisse zeigen: Ein solcher virtueller Begleiter, der durch die App führt und deren Funktionen Schritt für Schritt erklärt, hat viel Potenzial, die Lernerfahrung bei der erstmaligen Nutzung der App zu verbessern.
In einer zweiten Studie prüfte Resch, wie visuelles Feedback zur Fußbelastung in unterschiedlichen virtuellen Umgebungen wahrgenommen wird. Auf welche Weise beeinflusst sie die Wahrnehmung des Feedbacks, das Gangbild und die User Experience?
„Virtual Reality bietet die Möglichkeit, solche Trainingssituationen auf dem Laufband interaktiv und kontrolliert zu gestalten und dabei die Interaktion mit smarten Geräten gezielt zu untersuchen“, lautet Reschs Fazit.
Welche Orthese würden Menschen gerne tragen?
Der dritte Forschungsschwerpunkt widmete sich dem Einfluss des Fußorthesen-Designs auf deren Akzeptanz. „Die technisch beste Orthese bringt nichts, wenn Menschen sie nicht tragen wollen“, sagt Resch. Er untersuchte zudem, wie generative KI für das Design und die Entwicklung solch medizinischer Hilfsmittel eingesetzt werden kann. „Der Weg zu einer marktfähigen Orthese ist natürlich noch weit“, resümiert der Forscher, „aber meine Untersuchungen geben erste Einblicke, wie KI-generierte Designs wahrgenommen werden und wie sich generative KI systematisch in einen Designprozess bis hin zur Prototypentwicklung einbinden lässt.“
Forschung für die Praxis auf erstklassigem Niveau
Resch hat in Kooperation mit der andalusischen Universidad de Cádiz promoviert, Erstbetreuer war Prof. Dr. Daniel Sánchez Morillo. An der Frankfurt UAS wurde seine Promotion von Prof. Dr. Diana Völz betreut, die verantwortlich für das Mixed-Reality-Labor ist.
„Stefan Reschs Forschung bedeutet für das Feld der Mensch-Technik-Interaktion im Bereich Personalized Medical Engineering einen großen Schritt vorwärts“, betont Völz, Professorin für Produktentwicklung, Konstruktion und CAD. „Die Universidad de Cádiz hat seine Leistung zu Recht mit der Bestnote ,Sobresaliente Cum Laude‘ gewürdigt – und unterstreicht damit, auf welch erstklassigem Niveau bei uns geforscht wird. Wir sind stolz darauf, dass wir Stefan Resch im Mixed-Reality-Labor das geeignete akademische Umfeld und die nötige Unterstützung für seinen Weg bieten konnten.“
¹ Stefan Reschs Dissertation „User-Centered Design and Evaluation of Smart Devices for Foot Augmentation: Interactive Mixed Reality Training and Feedback Applications“ fasst die Ergebnisse mehrerer Artikel zusammen, die bereits in wissenschaftlichen Fachzeitschriften veröffentlicht, auf internationalen Fachkonferenzen präsentiert und durch Auszeichnungen gewürdigt wurden. Vertreterinnen und Vertreter der Hochschule Aalen sowie der IHK Ostwürttemberg freuen sich über die Auszeichnung Ostwürttembergs als „Leuchtturm-Region MINTernational“.

Ostwürttemberg ist „Leuchtturm-Region MINTernational“: Der Stifterverband für die Deutsche Wissenschaft e.V. hat die gemeinsame Bewerbung der Hochschule Aalen und der IHK Ostwürttemberg ausgewählt. Zusammen mit Partnern aus Wirtschaft und Verwaltung wollen sie mehr internationale Studierende aus den MINT-Fächern (Mathematik, Informatik, Naturwissenschaften und Technik) nach dem Abschluss als Fachkräfte in der Region halten. Dafür gibt es 50.000 Euro Förderung.
Mit dem Programm „Leuchttürme MINTernational“ zeichnet der Stifterverband Regionen aus, in denen Hochschulen, Unternehmen und Behörden gemeinsam internationaler MINT-Studierender beim Berufseinstig unterstützen. In Ostwürttemberg knüpft das Vorhaben an die gewachsene Zusammenarbeit in der Region an, etwa in der Fachkräfteallianz Ostwürttemberg, im Welcome Center Ostwürttemberg und in der regionalen MINT-Initiative, mit der sich Ostwürttemberg als MINT-Modellregion Baden-Württembergs positioniert. Nun soll der Übergang vom Studium in den Beruf gezielt gestärkt werden: Internationale Studierende bringen gefragte Kompetenzen mit – und können so zur Zukunft der Unternehmen in Ostwürttemberg beitragen.
„Mit unserem Masterstudiengang Datenmanagement in Produktentwicklung und Produktion an der Hochschule Aalen bilden wir gezielt Fachkräfte für eine zentrale Herausforderung des Maschinenbaus aus: Künstlicher Intelligenz so einzusetzen, dass industrielle Abläufe effizienter werden“, sagt Studiendekanin Prof. Dr. Doris Aschenbrenner. Internationale Studierende seien für die technologische Zukunft der Region immens wichtig. „Umso mehr freuen wir uns, dass wir die bereits enge Zusammenarbeit unseres Studiengangs mit der IHK durch die Förderung als MINT-Leuchtturm weiter ausbauen können. Unser Ziel ist es, internationale Talente nicht nur für ein Studium in Aalen zu gewinnen, sondern ihnen gemeinsam mit den regionalen Unternehmen auch langfristige berufliche Perspektiven zu eröffnen.“
Prof. Dr. Anja Dieckmann, Prorektorin für Internationales und Kommunikation der Hochschule Aalen, ergänzt: „Internationale Studierende sind für unsere Region ein enormer Gewinn – kulturell, fachlich und wirtschaftlich. Die Förderung als MINT-Leuchtturm helfe dabei, ihnen den Berufseinstieg zu erleichtern.
Schon heute gibt es vielfältige Angebote: Von Orientierungswochen, Deutschkursen und Buddy-Programmen an der Hochschule über die Beratung im Welcome Center bis hin zu Unternehmensbesuchen mit dem JOB-BUS und dem Programm MINTconnect International. Künftig sollen die Angebote besser gebündelt und sichtbarer werden. Geplant sind ein digitaler „MINT Talent Hub“ mit Praktikums- und Einstiegsbörse, ein Karriereprogramm mit Bewerbungstraining und berufsbezogenem Deutsch, Mentoring sowie ein jährliches „MINT Talent Forum“.
„Die Auszeichnung ist ein gutes Signal für ganz Ostwürttemberg: Hochschule, Unternehmen und IHK zeigen gemeinsam, wie internationale Talente in der Region ankommen und bleiben können. Unsere Unternehmen brauchen diese Fachkräfte“, sagt Thilo Rentschler, Hauptgeschäftsführer der IHK Ostwürttemberg. Hochschule, Wirtschaft und Verwaltung arbeiten dabei Hand in Hand: Die Hochschule Aalen übernimmt den Kontakt zu den Studierenden, ihre Qualifizierung und die wissenschaftliche Begleitung. Die IHK Ostwürttemberg und das Welcome Center Ostwürttemberg bringen Studierende und Unternehmen zusammen. Weitere Partner sind die J. Rettenmaier & Söhne GmbH + Co. KG und das Landratsamt Ostalbkreis.
Eine berufliche Zukunft in Ostwürttemberg können sich auch Adrian Rojas und Sharon Vásquez vorstellen. Die beiden kommen aus Costa Rica, haben bei Prof. Dr. Doris Aschenbrenner ihre Bachelorarbeit geschrieben und studieren inzwischen den Masterstudiengang Advanced Materials and Manufacturing an der Hochschule Aalen: „MINT voranzubringen ist wichtig – und MINTernational zeigt, wie internationale Studierende und Unternehmen dabei zusammenfinden können“, sagt der 24-Jährige. Und seine 25-jährige Kommilitonin fügt hinzu: „Wir finden das Programm großartig, es ist eine tolle Unterstützung. Nach unserem Master können wir uns gut vorstellen, als Fachkräfte in Ostwürttemberg einzusteigen und unser Wissen hier einzubringen.“
